title: Simultaneous Effect Identification across All Minimum-Edge DAG I-Maps from a Conditional-Independence Oracle
banked_reason: Math review passes, but the contribution remains a generic finite enumeration plus real-closed-field feasibility composition; the negative strictness witness does not prove a stronger identification region.
gap_reasons: The main completeness theorem establishes decidability through exhaustive DAG enumeration and generic real-closed-field quantifier elimination, but supplies no degree, height, certificate-length, or usable runtime bound.
The sole worked cross-MEC example produces an ambiguity certificate rather than a common effect missed by existing graphical criteria.
General separating tables are only real algebraic, while rational replacement and effective height control remain explicitly open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact finite procedure that enumerates tied sparsest DAGs, decides pairwise effect equality over the positive exact-oracle chamber by real-closed-field methods, computes the maximal effect quotient, and returns exact algebraic separators; it also verified the explicit four-node rational ambiguity witness and fixed-class Wald inference. The advertised bounded rational-positive separator theorem collapsed because saturated-ideal nonmembership need not select the relevant positive sign chamber or a rational point. A field-tier successor must prove effective rational replacement with height bounds and/or construct a substantive positive cross-MEC common-effect example beyond existing graphical criteria.
tldr: SparseSIM-ID starts from finite state spaces, a complete exact conditional-independence oracle, background orientations, and a causal query; a rational realization and a compressed graph family are optional checked accelerators. It certifies oracle realizability, exhaustively constructs every minimum-edge DAG I-map, and invokes exact pairwise positive-chamber decisions to compute the unique coarsest quotient whose classes share \(P_x(Y)\) on the strictly positive exact-oracle model. Each pairwise decision returns either a finite universal-equality certificate or an exact real-algebraic positive ambiguity table. Normalization reduces the all-pairs decision count to \(\binom{|\mathfrak D|}{2}(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\), and the reference-only common-effect test to \((|\mathfrak D|-1)(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\). For every fixed or externally certified true quotient class \(C\), the representative circuit supports a multivariate plug-in central limit theorem, consistent sandwich covariance, and Wald intervals for fixed contrasts; this is not inference after data-driven oracle or class selection. The explicit four-binary-variable rational cross-MEC witness remains a strictness certificate.
gap: Existing simultaneous-identification theory gives sufficient graphical conditions but not a necessary common-law test or a positive rational failure witness for tied sparsest outputs.
fill: The project restricts attention to checkably nonempty certified inputs, isolates and proves an effect-specific rational-positive separation theorem, packages it into an exhaustive certificate algorithm with explicit size bounds, proves strictness over the closest sufficient graphical test on a certified rational witness, and attaches fixed-input plug-in inference with an explicit sandwich covariance to the common circuit.
